opening.text: A potter shapes a bowl from soft clay. It looks done. But it isn't. It still has to go into the kiln. The heat is fierce. The clay can't see why. But without the fire, the bowl would crumble the first time someone used it. Trials can feel like that kiln. And the Potter knows what He is making.

mainMessage.text: Trials are the kiln that makes us strong enough to be used.

blocks.text: **No one skips the kiln** Every bowl goes through the fire. Every life has hard days.
Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you:
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
Each of us will face adversity no matter where we are.
No one skips it.
**Part of the plan** The kiln isn't a mistake. It's part of how the bowl is made.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard is part of the gospel plan.
It's part of the plan.
**Stronger after the fire** A fired bowl holds water. An unfired one doesn't. Hard things can make us strong.
Nevertheless, Jacob, my firstborn in the wilderness, thou knowest the greatness of God; and he shall consecrate thine afflictions for thy gain.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard makes us stronger, humbles us, and gives us a chance to prove ourselves.
Hard makes us stronger.
**We may not see why** The clay can't see the Potter's plan. We often can't see ours either. But growth is still happening.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We may never know in this life why we face what we do, but we can feel confident that we can grow from the experience.
We can still grow.
**Through the water and fire** The Lord doesn't say we won't pass through hard places. He says He'll be with us in them. So we go forward in faith.

When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
The Lord’s answer to hard times is to go forward with faith.
Go forward in faith.
**Trust the Potter** The clay does best when it stays in the Potter's hands. We do best when we trust the Savior.

And now, O my son Helaman, behold, thou art in thy youth, and therefore, I beseech of thee that thou wilt hear my words and learn of me; for I do know that whosoever shall put their trust in God shall be supported in their trials, and their troubles, and their afflictions, and shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We need to follow the example of the Savior and trust in Him.
Trust Him.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a hard season shaped them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph in prison

blocks.text: Joseph had done nothing wrong. He was put in prison anyway.

And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison. But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
The prison was Joseph's kiln. But the Lord was with him there. And later, that hard season prepared him to bless many people.

application.text: First, name one hard thing you are in right now. Second, ask Heavenly Father what He wants you to learn from it. Third, take one step of faith this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know hard times are not a sign that God has left us. I know Jesus Christ is with us in the fire. I know He is making something good of us. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Nobody builds muscle by lifting nothing. The weights feel heavy. The arms shake. It's no fun in the moment. But a week, a month, a year later, the person can carry what once felt impossible. Trials are a lot like that gym. The weight is real. So is the strength it builds.

mainMessage.text: Trials are the weights that build spiritual strength.

blocks.text: **Everyone lifts something** No one gets a weightless life. Each of us carries something heavy.
Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you:
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
Each of us will face adversity no matter where we are.
Everyone lifts something.
**The trainer planned the workout** A good trainer picks the weight on purpose. God knows what we can carry, and He is part of the plan.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard is part of the gospel plan.
It's in the plan.
**The reps pay off** Strength comes from the work, not from avoiding it. Hard things build us up.
Nevertheless, Jacob, my firstborn in the wilderness, thou knowest the greatness of God; and he shall consecrate thine afflictions for thy gain.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard makes us stronger, humbles us, and gives us a chance to prove ourselves.
Hard builds strength.
**Soreness isn't damage** Sore muscles can feel like something went wrong. Often it's growth. We may not know why we hurt, but we can trust we're growing.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We may never know in this life why we face what we do, but we can feel confident that we can grow from the experience.
Growth can feel like pain.
**One more rep** When we want to quit, the answer isn't to put the weight down. It's to keep going, with the Lord beside us.

When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
The Lord’s answer to hard times is to go forward with faith.
Keep going.
**A spotter** Good lifters have a spotter. We have the Savior. He doesn't take the weight away. He keeps us from being crushed.

And now, O my son Helaman, behold, thou art in thy youth, and therefore, I beseech of thee that thou wilt hear my words and learn of me; for I do know that whosoever shall put their trust in God shall be supported in their trials, and their troubles, and their afflictions, and shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We need to follow the example of the Savior and trust in Him.
He spots us.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when carrying something hard made them stronger. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Job

blocks.text: Job lost his children, his wealth and his health. He still did not let go of God.

Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord. For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
Job didn't understand why. But he knew his Redeemer lived. That one truth held the whole weight.

application.text: First, think of a trial you've been trying to avoid. Second, ask the Lord to help you carry it, not just escape it. Third, write down one way you've grown because of it.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know my Redeemer lives. I know Jesus Christ helps us carry what we can't carry alone. I know trials can make us stronger. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Bread dough gets pushed, folded and pressed. It gets punched down. If dough could talk, it would say, "Why is this happening to me?" But without all that kneading, there would be no loaf. Just a sticky lump. Hard times can feel like the kneading. They are not the end of the story.

mainMessage.text: Trials knead us into something better than we were.

blocks.text: **Everyone gets kneaded** No dough skips it. No life does either.
Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you:
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
Each of us will face adversity no matter where we are.
Everyone is kneaded.
**The Baker has a plan** The baker has a loaf in mind. The Lord has a plan for us too, and the hard parts belong to it.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard is part of the gospel plan.
The Baker has a plan.
**Firm and humble** Kneading makes dough firm and ready to rise. Hard things make us stronger and more humble.
Nevertheless, Jacob, my firstborn in the wilderness, thou knowest the greatness of God; and he shall consecrate thine afflictions for thy gain.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard makes us stronger, humbles us, and gives us a chance to prove ourselves.
Stronger and humbler.
**Rest before the rise** After kneading, dough rests under a cloth. It looks like nothing is happening. But it's rising. We may not know why we wait, but growth is happening.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We may never know in this life why we face what we do, but we can feel confident that we can grow from the experience.
Growing while we wait.
**Into the oven with faith** The oven is the hottest part. We don't pull out of it early. We go forward in faith, and the Lord goes with us.

When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
The Lord’s answer to hard times is to go forward with faith.
Stay in with faith.
**Bread to share** In the end, the loaf feeds others. A life shaped by trials can bless others who are struggling. The Savior is our example.

And now, O my son Helaman, behold, thou art in thy youth, and therefore, I beseech of thee that thou wilt hear my words and learn of me; for I do know that whosoever shall put their trust in God shall be supported in their trials, and their troubles, and their afflictions, and shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We need to follow the example of the Savior and trust in Him.
Follow Him and trust Him.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a hard season made them better able to help others. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Alma and his people in bondage

blocks.text: Alma's people were under cruel rulers. They prayed. The Lord answered.

And I will also ease the burdens which are put upon your shoulders, that even you cannot feel them upon your backs, even while you are in bondage; and this will I do that ye may stand as witnesses for me hereafter, and that ye may know of a surety that I, the Lord God, do visit my people in their afflictions. And now it came to pass that the burdens which were laid upon Alma and his brethren were made light; yea, the Lord did strengthen them that they could bear up their burdens with ease, and they did submit cheerfully and with patience to all the will of the Lord.
The burdens weren't taken away at first. They were made light. The Lord visited them in their trial.

application.text: First, think of someone who has been through something hard and came out kind. Second, ask what they learned. Third, share something you've learned with someone who is struggling now.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Lord visits His people in their afflictions. I know Jesus Christ can make heavy burdens light. I know hard times can make us more kind. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: In winter, a tree looks dead. The branches are bare. The wind whips through. Nothing green anywhere. But the roots are growing deeper. And when spring comes, the tree is ready. Trials can feel like winter. But something is happening below the surface.

mainMessage.text: Trials are winter seasons. The roots grow deepest when it's cold.

blocks.text: **Winter comes to every tree** No tree skips winter. No one skips hard seasons.
Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you:
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
Each of us will face adversity no matter where we are.
Winter comes to all.
**Winter is a season, not a mistake** Seasons are part of how a tree lives. Hard times are part of how we live.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard is part of the gospel plan.
It's a season.
**Deep roots** A tree in a storm holds on by its roots. Hard times make ours go down deeper.
Nevertheless, Jacob, my firstborn in the wilderness, thou knowest the greatness of God; and he shall consecrate thine afflictions for thy gain.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard makes us stronger, humbles us, and gives us a chance to prove ourselves.
Roots grow deeper.
**Growth we can't see** The tree doesn't explain why it needs winter. We may not understand our winters either. But we can trust that we're growing.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We may never know in this life why we face what we do, but we can feel confident that we can grow from the experience.
Growing underground.
**Spring is coming** The tree doesn't give up in January. It waits, it holds on. We go forward with faith, and the Lord is with us.

When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
The Lord’s answer to hard times is to go forward with faith.
Hold on for spring.
**Rooted in Christ** The deepest roots go into good soil. We root ourselves in the Savior and trust Him.

And now, O my son Helaman, behold, thou art in thy youth, and therefore, I beseech of thee that thou wilt hear my words and learn of me; for I do know that whosoever shall put their trust in God shall be supported in their trials, and their troubles, and their afflictions, and shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We need to follow the example of the Savior and trust in Him.
Root in Christ.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a hard season turned out to have a purpose. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Paul’s hard years

blocks.text: Paul was beaten, shipwrecked and jailed. Yet he wrote this:
We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;
Paul didn't say it was easy. He said it wasn't the end. Troubled, but not distressed. Cast down, but not destroyed.

application.text: First, ask yourself what season you're in right now. Second, name one thing you can do to stay rooted in Christ, such as prayer or scripture study. Third, do it daily this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know spring follows winter. I know Jesus Christ is the root that holds us. I know we are cast down but not destroyed. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Driving into a long mountain tunnel, the light behind you fades. Ahead is dim. For a moment you may feel closed in. But you don't stop the car in the middle. You keep driving, because you know tunnels end. Trials can feel like a tunnel. The way out is forward.

mainMessage.text: Trials are a tunnel. We get through by going forward in faith.

blocks.text: **Every road has a tunnel** No one drives a long road without one. No one lives without hard stretches.
Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you:
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
Each of us will face adversity no matter where we are.
Everyone drives through one.
**Built into the route** The tunnel is part of the road. Hard times are part of the gospel plan.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard is part of the gospel plan.
It's on the route.
**What the dark teaches** In the dark, we pay closer attention. We lean on the headlights. Hard times can teach us to lean on the Lord.
Nevertheless, Jacob, my firstborn in the wilderness, thou knowest the greatness of God; and he shall consecrate thine afflictions for thy gain.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
Hard makes us stronger, humbles us, and gives us a chance to prove ourselves.
The dark teaches us.
**The end we can't yet see** Inside the tunnel, we can't see the exit. We may not know why we're in it. But we can trust the road leads out.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We may never know in this life why we face what we do, but we can feel confident that we can grow from the experience.
The road leads out.
**Keep driving** The worst thing is to stop in the middle. We keep going, with the Lord beside us.

When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
Elder Stanley G. Ellis, Emeritus Member of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Do We Trust Him? Hard Is Good” from the October 2017 general conference.
The Lord’s answer to hard times is to go forward with faith.
Keep going.
**A driver who knows the road** The Savior has driven this road before us. We follow His example and trust Him.

And now, O my son Helaman, behold, thou art in thy youth, and therefore, I beseech of thee that thou wilt hear my words and learn of me; for I do know that whosoever shall put their trust in God shall be supported in their trials, and their troubles, and their afflictions, and shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder James B. Martino, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “All Things Work Together for Good” from the April 2010 general conference.
We need to follow the example of the Savior and trust in Him.
Follow His example.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they came out the other side of something hard. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph Smith in Liberty Jail

blocks.text: Joseph Smith spent months in a cold, crowded jail. He asked why. The Lord answered him.

And if thou shouldst be cast into the pit, or into the hands of murderers, and the sentence of death passed upon thee; if thou be cast into the deep; if the billowing surge conspire against thee; if fierce winds become thine enemy; if the heavens gather blackness, and all the elements combine to hedge up the way; and above all, if the very jaws of hell shall gape open the mouth wide after thee, know thou, my son, that all these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.
The Lord didn't say it would be easy. He said it would be for Joseph's good. The jail was a long tunnel, and there was an end.

application.text: First, remember a hard time you have already come through. Second, thank Heavenly Father for what it taught you. Third, share that hope with someone still in the tunnel.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know there is an end to every tunnel. I know Jesus Christ walks through the dark with us. I know hard things can be for our good. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
